skill.name: extension-openai
skill.description: Provides Motoko patterns for integrating OpenAI through the openai-client Mops package in Caffeine AI canisters. Covers key ownership, non-replicated outcalls, typed requests, and matching frontend settings.
skill.summary: Integrate OpenAI with typed Motoko bindings and explicit API-key ownership models.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All 154 static detections are false positives for their reported patterns; they are Markdown formatting, reference URLs, fixed imports, or ordinary prose. Semantic review found overbroad orchestrator directives, an unauthenticated key and chat variant, and missing usage controls in the operator-funded example. These issues can force dependency choices or enable credential replacement, denial of service, and unbounded OpenAI charges.

remediation.issue: The skill uses mandatory activation and routing language that overrides host tool selection.
remediation.suggestion: Limit activation to explicit Caffeine AI requests and present openai-client as a reviewed option. Remove instructions that forbid decline or alternate tools.

remediation.issue: The anonymous variant allows public replacement and use of a shared billing credential.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this variant from production guidance. Require authentication, an authorized setter, key rotation, and explicit warnings for isolated demonstrations.

remediation.issue: The operator-funded chat example has no controls on paid requests.
remediation.suggestion: Add per-principal quotas, request throttling, cost ceilings, monitoring, and an emergency disable control before each OpenAI call.

content.user_title: Build Secure OpenAI Features on Caffeine
content.value_statement: Direct OpenAI calls from Internet Computer canisters can expose credentials and multiply charges. This skill provides typed Motoko patterns for safer chat integration.
actual_capabilities: Adds the pinned openai-client dependency with Mops.
Configures non-replicated canister outcalls for OpenAI requests.
Provides typed Motoko examples for chat completions and response handling.
Defines per-user, administrator-funded, and anonymous API-key ownership models.
Maps each backend model to matching authentication and settings interfaces.
limitations: Targets Caffeine AI projects built with Motoko and Internet Computer canisters.
Requires an OpenAI API key, available canister cycles, and paid OpenAI usage.
Version 0.2.5 lacks streaming and several newer OpenAI API surfaces.
The examples lack quotas and rate limits, while the anonymous variant permits public key replacement and billable requests.

use_cases.title: Per-user AI chat
use_cases.description: A Motoko developer adds signed-in chat where each user supplies and funds a separate OpenAI key.

use_cases.title: Operator-funded assistant
use_cases.description: A SaaS operator configures one protected key for authenticated users and adds application-level spending controls.

use_cases.title: Integration security review
use_cases.description: A security engineer checks key exposure, caller gates, replication settings, and unsupported API requirements before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Add OpenAI chat
prompt_templates.prompt: Add OpenAI chat to my Caffeine AI project. Use per-user keys, typed openai-client bindings, and a settings page.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a basic authenticated chat feature.

prompt_templates.title: Choose key ownership
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose an API-key ownership model for this project: [requirements]. Compare per-user, administrator-funded, and anonymous options with security and billing tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design funded access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an administrator-funded OpenAI chat feature for [application]. Include role gates, per-user quotas, rate limits, cost ceilings, and configuration status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a production service using one operator key.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Motoko OpenAI integration for raw HTTP calls, key exposure, replicated outcalls, missing caller checks, unsupported APIs, and unbounded spending.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review an existing implementation before deployment.

output_examples.input: Add OpenAI chat to a signed-in application with several independent users.
output: Selected the per-user key model because the application has login and multiple users.
Planned authenticated key setup, configuration status, key removal, and chat screens.
Required non-replicated calls and typed openai-client requests.
High risk: authenticated users can submit unlimited operator-funded requests.
Recommended per-user quotas, request throttling, usage monitoring, and a global spending limit.
Confirmed that no endpoint returns the stored key.

output_examples.input: Use real-time streaming responses with the pinned connector.
output: The pinned connector does not support Realtime or streaming.
Use a supported non-streaming flow or choose another reviewed integration.

best_practices: Default to per-user keys when ownership and billing responsibility are not explicit.
Keep keys server-side, expose only configuration status, and never log or return credentials.
Enforce non-replicated outcalls, usage limits, and cost monitoring before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not build raw OpenAI HTTP requests or hand-written response parsing.
Do not expose API-key getters, browser storage, logs, or telemetry containing credentials.
Do not deploy anonymous or shared-key access without strict quotas and explicit risk acceptance.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets Caffeine AI applications using Motoko and Internet Computer canisters.

faq.question: Does the skill call OpenAI automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples for applications that call OpenAI after key configuration.

faq.question: Which key ownership models are included?
faq.answer: It covers per-user keys, one administrator-managed key, and an unsafe anonymous shared-key variant.

faq.question: Does the connector support streaming?
faq.answer: No. The documented connector returns complete responses and does not support Realtime or server-sent events.

faq.question: Which dependency is required?
faq.answer: The instructions use openai-client version 0.2.5 or later through the Mops package manager.

faq.question: Is the anonymous variant suitable for production?
faq.answer: No. Any visitor can replace the key and make billable requests, so production deployments need authentication and usage limits.
